title: Testing S-Shaped and Closed Loop Curves with the Vertical Line Test
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Vertical Line Test
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Examine two curves in the first quadrant: (a) a curve shaped like the numeral 2 that arches up, slants diagonally backward to the left, and then extends horizontally to the right; (b) a closed oval loop lying entirely in the first quadrant. Determine whether either curve is the graph of a function of x.
finalAnswer: \text{(a) Not a function of } x; \quad \text{(b) Not a function of } x

steps.title: Recall the Uniqueness Condition for Functions
steps.explanation: For a curve to represent a function y = f(x), each x-value in the domain must correspond to a single y-value, meaning no vertical line can intersect the curve at two or more distinct points.
steps.why: A relation that assigns multiple outputs to a single input is a multi-valued relation, not a function.

steps.title: Analyze Curve (a)
steps.mathExpression: x = c \text{ intersects curve (a) up to } 3 \text{ times}
steps.explanation: In curve (a), the middle diagonal segment slants backward from right to left underneath the upper arch and above the lower horizontal segment. A vertical line through this central region intersects the curve at three distinct y-values.
steps.why: Any curve that reverses horizontal direction and overlaps its x-interval fails the Vertical Line Test.

steps.title: Analyze Curve (b)
steps.mathExpression: x = c \text{ intersects the closed loop (b) in } 2 \text{ points}
steps.explanation: In curve (b), the graph forms a closed oval loop. Any vertical line passing through the interior of the loop intersects both the top boundary and the bottom boundary, giving two distinct y-values for each x.
steps.why: Every closed loop in the plane encloses an open interval of x-values where each vertical line crosses the boundary at least twice.

steps.title: Summarize Findings
steps.mathExpression: \text{Neither (a) nor (b) is the graph of a function of } x
steps.explanation: Both graphs fail the Vertical Line Test because vertical lines intersect graph (a) up to three times and graph (b) twice.
steps.why: Failing the Vertical Line Test on any subinterval disqualifies the entire curve from being a function of x.
